caveats: Years left are a projection of the recent (2011-2026, weather-normalised) decline rate; they are not a forecast of what farmers or water managers will do. The hindcast shows declines can speed up or slow down by decade.

The headline depends on the years used for the trend: region p50 at 30 ft is 59 years with 2001-2026, 69 with 2011-2026 (used) and 77 with 2016-2026. 2011-2013 was the pumping peak; 2016-2025 pumping averaged 28% less, so the clock may lean short if that holds.
Saturated thickness at a field is uncertain by roughly +/-20-30 ft because the aquifer base map is coarse (1:1,000,000, 200-ft contours plus KGS bedrock picks).
0 years means the central estimate is already below the threshold; many wells still pump below 30 ft of saturated thickness, at reduced capacity.
100 means 100 years or more (flat or rising water levels).
County clocks summarise the groundwater-irrigated points of diversion (WIMAS) weighted by reported acres.
GRACE sees a footprint of a few hundred kilometres; its 2003-2026 storage trend is about 1/4 of the well-based trend here (Sy 0.15), so it is used as a timing / sign check, not to scale the clock.
Income uses ERS regional costs that do not separate irrigated from dryland farms and excludes pumping energy; irrigated yields after 2018 are estimated from earlier NASS ratios.
Wallace County is kept in GMD4 as in the contract list, although 90% of its irrigated acres lie inside the GMD1 polygon (econ module check).
This is decision support, not a replacement for your agronomist or for local water-right rules.
